title: Stepwise retirement of legacy SSE & polling endpoints — client impact playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: This PRD defines a staged deprecation plan for two legacy transport surfaces used by long-running clients: the Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming endpoint and the polling-based generate endpoint variant. The goal is to migrate customers to the unified multiplexed streaming API and the consolidated /generate endpoint variants that support streaming, structured output, and automated fallbacks. We aim to minimize customer disruption while reclaiming maintenance costs and simplifying the runtime surface.
background: Over the past 18 months usage of the legacy SSE endpoint and a handful of client-side polling patterns has declined while maintenance burden and cross-cutting complexity (rate-limiting, routing, observability) have increased. Several runtime optimizations and telemetry pipelines are only applied to the new streaming surface; maintaining parity across both surfaces consumes significant engineering cycles and hides regressions.
goals: 1) Provide a low-friction upgrade path for existing customers using SSE and polling. 2) Retire legacy endpoints within a 12-week phased window. 3) Ensure >= 99.9% continuity for active customers during migration. 4) Reduce surface area for operational runbooks and runtime complexity.
out_of_scope: Rewriting client SDKs to force migration; custom on-prem/private deployments tied to discrete contractual obligations (those are handled case-by-case). Backwards-incompatible payload model changes unrelated to transport behavior.
requirements: 1. Clear, scriptable migration steps and a compatibility shim for 8 weeks post-deprecation. 2. Telemetry to detect remaining legacy clients by token, endpoint, and SDK version. 3. Automated opt-in for customers that have no streaming-compatible model variants. 4. Communication templates and a self-serve migration dashboard in Console.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Migration docs published and linked from Console by week 2. 2) Migration SDK samples (Node/Python) validated with integration tests and published to repos. 3) Telemetry shows a steady decline of legacy endpoint usage to <5% at week 8 and <1% at week 12. 4) No customer-experienced outage attributable to the migration: incidents caused by the migration must be resolved with severity<=P2 and documented. 5) Console shows per-customer migration status; at least 90% of customers with >1k monthly requests have either migrated or have approved exceptions by week 10.
migration_plan: Week 0: Announce deprecation timeline (12 weeks) via email, Console banner, and changelog. Publish migration playbook and SDK examples.
Week 1-2: Instrumentation & telemetry rollout — token-scoped usage dashboards; opt-out flags for risky changes; provide migration sandbox in Console.
Week 3-4: Provide compatibility shim: inbound proxy that rewrites legacy SSE/polling requests to new streaming surface for best-effort compatibility (8-week support window). Monitor for edge cases.
Week 5-7: Proactive outreach to high-usage accounts (top 100 by legacy traffic); offer guided migration sessions and temporary dedicated support channels.
Week 8: Disable non-essential legacy features (e.g., undocumented query params). Keep shim active but announce removal date for shim.
Week 9-11: Enforce server-side throttles and routing changes that preferentially route new traffic to unified endpoints. Continue outreach.
Week 12: Remove compatibility shim and return 410 for legacy endpoints with migration instructions and automatic error codes for clients. Post-mortem and closeout.
Post-deprecation (4 weeks): Final monitoring; keep a limited historical log for customer support; update docs to mark endpoints as retired.
communication_plan: 1) Initial announcement: 12-week deprecation notice with migration resources and link to sandbox. 2) Weekly progress emails to affected customers (by token owners) with their migration status. 3) Console: persistent banner + per-organization migration card with recommended next steps. 4) PR and changelog updates for public roadmap transparency. 5) Support: dedicated Slack channel and scheduled office hours for top 50 customers.
console_requirements: - Per-token migration status card with detected legacy usage and suggested code samples. - Ability for support to mark exceptions or request extended shim windows. - Migration sandbox that mirrors production routing but with test quotas.
monitoring_and_success_metrics: - Percent of requests served to legacy endpoints by week. - Number of active tokens still calling legacy endpoints. - Number of migration-related incidents and their severities. - Time-to-migration for top 20 customers. - Customer satisfaction (NPS touchpoint after migration for supported customers).
rollback_and_fallback: If telemetry indicates a regression impacting >0.1% of production traffic or a P1 incident, we will: 1) Re-enable compatibility shim and revert API gateway rule changes. 2) Open an incident channel with engineering, PM, and SRE. 3) Communicate status to affected customers within 30 minutes of detection. A rollback runbook will be maintained in the SRE playbooks repo.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Some customers run older SDKs that cannot talk to the new streaming API. Mitigation: Compatibility shim + targeted outreach + provide backported SDK patches.
Risk: Migration causes increased token-level throttling or unexpected latency. Mitigation: Staged throttling, canary traffic shifts, and per-token autoscaling allowances for migration windows.
Risk: Misrouted telemetry undercounts legacy usage. Mitigation: Dual instrumentation during Week 1-3 and sampling checks against raw ingress logs.
Risk: Enterprise customers on Private deployments are contractually unable to change endpoints. Mitigation: Engage account teams early; treat these as exceptions with bespoke migration schedules.
open_questions: 1) Should the compatibility shim be available for Private deployments by default, or treated as a paid migration service? 2) Do we allow customers to request extended shim windows beyond 8 weeks (preliminary answer: yes, for enterprise with approval). 3) What is the exact deprecation wording to avoid regulatory issues in EEA customers? Legal to sign off.
